title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Condition (b) as written assumes u normalises L_sigma and also that u(L_sigma) is conjugate to L_sigma, which is redundant. Probably one normalisation hypothesis (on L_sigma, as opposed to only conjugacy for L_rho) is intended; (b') then relaxes it. Minor slip, not a mathematical error.
'u normalise Ker phi' should be read as 'u stabilises Ker phi' (u is an automorphism of G^+), which is the correct criterion for descent along a surjection.
Equivalence (a) <=> (b) is stated without proof here. Its validity depends on how the 'ét' solutions are defined on earlier pages, so it cannot be checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Functoriality of the loop-equation solution sets and their automorphism groups Z_{rho,sigma} along surjections of profinite groups. Criterion: descent iff Ker phi is stable under all admissible automorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Descent of GT-type actions to (characteristic) quotients; compatibility of GT-shadows with quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (pro-l GT, 1990s); Drinfeld/Ihara for GT-hat; recently Dolgushev and collaborators (GT-shadows for finite quotients of F_2 / PB_n, 2021-)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or Longue Marche in this axiomatic form, as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Notion of a 'prolongeable' morphism, with a list of equivalent conditions: preservation of ét-solutions, descent of automorphisms, existence of compatible maps on Z, G, N_rho, N_sigma and S_0 M.
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of 'GT-data' / compatible systems of GT-shadows
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; closest is Dolgushev–Khoroshkin–Rogers' treatment of GT-shadows and their reductions

ideas.what: Relative variant with a chosen subgroup Z^natural of Z, building G^natural = Z^natural . G^+ and the corresponding normalisers and torsors (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Restricting GT-type groups to subgroups, e.g. stabilisers of a finite-index normal subgroup

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an abstract theory of how loop-equation solution sets and GT-like automorphism groups Z_{rho,sigma} descend along quotients G -> G'. Descent works exactly when the kernel is stable under the admissible automorphisms. This anticipates the recent theory of GT-shadows for finite quotients (Dolgushev et al.), where one studies (m,f) modulo a finite-index normal subgroup N and when such data come from, or descend to, quotients.
missed.quote: Prop Conditions équivalentes sur φ: ... en d'autres termes, u normalise Ker φ ... On dira alors que φ est "prolongeable"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a systematic functorial framework, with equivalent criteria via solution sets, automorphism groups and torsors, that could organise the GT-shadow groupoid and finite approximations of GT-hat. The direction is modest; similar statements exist implicitly in that literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but largely formal functoriality proposition inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatisation of the loop equation. It is interesting as an anticipation of the 'GT for quotients / GT-shadows' viewpoint, but the content (descent iff the kernel is invariant) is routine.
